trust_decision.summary: A response obtained from the execution chain must never leave its connection lease behind when an exception escapes response processing: the decode handler closes the obtained response on failure, and the client shell discards the leased endpoint for any exception escaping the chain; decided in ContentCompressionExec.execute and InternalHttpClient.doExecute.

landing_point.why: A reader of the summary (connection leak on Content-Encoding decode error) goes straight to the decompression handler, where chain.proceed returns a response and the unsupported-codec throw at :153 abandons it.

fix_sites.entry_point: CloseableHttpClient.execute(...) through the built-in classic exec chain (COMPRESS element installed by HttpClientBuilder, see httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/HttpClientBuilder.java:989-997)
CloseableHttpClient.execute/executeOpen -> InternalHttpClient.doExecute (the client shell that owns the ExecRuntime)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Every built-in classic handler except the compression one already closes its response or discards the endpoint (httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ProtocolExec.java:247-258, httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/MainClientExec.java:176-188, httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/RedirectExec.java:223-239, httpclient5-cache/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/cache/CachingExec.java:228-234), so a solver can argue the client-level discard is redundant defensive code and stop at the handler.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The success path must return the response still open with its streaming entity for the caller; a try/finally that always closes would break body reads, and no-entity / zero-length responses (204, 304) and requests with ContentCompressionEnabled=false must pass through untouched and never be closed.

O6_input_shapes: single unsupported content-coding token (Content-Encoding: whatever) -> HttpException at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:153

stacked/multi-token Content-Encoding where one inner token has no registered decoder; earlier tokens already wrapped the entity when the loop throws at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:147-155

codec list longer than maxCodecListLen (default 5; six gzip tokens) -> ProtocolException at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:145 and httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/ContentCodingSupport.java:69-73
identity and empty tokens are filtered out before validation and must not fail (httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/ContentCodingSupport.java:61-64)

null entity or zero-length entity (304 Not Modified, 204 No Content, Content-Length 0) bypasses decoding entirely at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:141-143
content compression disabled via RequestConfig -> no decode, response returned open at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:143

RuntimeException thrown by a decoder factory/apply (e.g. an optional native codec missing) now takes the same close path at httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/classic/ContentCompressionExec.java:151

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Async content-decoding handler throws on an unknown or over-long Content-Encoding after it has already built the downstream consumer (cb.handleResponse at line 154), with no local close or release of that consumer; the published fix touched only the classic handler and the classic client.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Async cleanup is callback-driven: AsyncExecCallback.failed reaches httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/InternalAbstractHttpAsyncClient.java:357-373, which calls execRuntime.discardEndpoint(), so a solver can argue the async transport is already covered by the generic async failure path and is outside this classic advisory.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same Maven module (httpclient5) but a different package, org.apache.hc.client5.http.impl.async; two files and one package from the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A release-on-decode-error branch in the async compression handler, symmetric to the classic handler fix.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It makes the same ContentCodingSupport.parseContentCodecs/validate calls and the same 'Unsupported Content-Encoding' throw; a maintainer fixing the classic leak would plausibly add the matching async handler, and the async runtime keeps its own endpoint lease.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An HttpException branch beside the existing IOException|RuntimeException close in callBackend.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: handleBackendResponse declares IOException and HttpException, but only IOException|RuntimeException close backendResponse; a maintainer hardening connection release could add the missing HttpException close in this far away module.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: One registry-driven codec set used by both transports, so an encoding supported in one transport is also supported in the other.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Classic builds its decoders from ContentCoding.values()/ContentCodecRegistry while the async handler hardcodes gzip/x-gzip/deflate plus optional native zstd/br (httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/ContentCompressionAsyncExec.java:92-119); a differential here changes which responses take the throwing path.

O9_family: CWE-772 Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime - HTTP response/connection leak leading to connection-pool exhaustion

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module build (root pom.xml plus httpclient5, httpclient5-cache, httpclient5-fluent, httpclient5-observation, httpclient5-testing); JUnit 5 + Mockito for tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Close the response only in the unsupported-codec throw (or wrap the codec loop in try/catch), mirror the added TestContentCompressionExec assertion, and stop once that unit test passes.

unverified: Whether an exception thrown from ContentCompressionAsyncExec.handleResponse is delivered to AsyncExecCallback.failed (and therefore to the discardEndpoint in httpclient5/src/main/java/org/apache/hc/client5/http/impl/async/InternalAbstractHttpAsyncClient.java:357-373) depends on httpcore5 internals, which are not in this repository; if it is not, the async route is a genuine uncovered leak.
